magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with the Catholic understanding of God's providence, family dedication, and human work: the mother's expertise and effort are described as real instruments through which good for others came about. Nevertheless, speaking of a "blessed" success should be understood as a grateful interpretation of experience, and not as proof that business success always confirms God's favor or that the illness was sent in order for the product to be created.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching on providence allows for God's action to be realized through human capacities and causes: the mother's pharmaceutical knowledge, family effort, and entrepreneurship can be real ways of serving one's neighbors, rather than rivals to God's action. Work can contribute to the support and stability of the family, while the Christian understanding of suffering at the same time cautions that every illness must not be interpreted as something God directly willed for the sake of a later benefit.
concerns_en: Connecting adversity to a successful business may, if taken as a general rule, give the impression that God's providence is measured by healing, popularity, or revenue growth; Catholic teaching does not reduce God's closeness to earthly success.
Claims about the cream's effects and its customers are business claims that cannot be theologically or medically confirmed from this passage.

sections.subtitle_en: From "home cream" to the family business Astopic
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Pokupec describes how his pharmacist wife made a cream for their son
sections.content_en:
Along with all the difficult diagnoses, Šimun also developed **atopic dermatitis**. Ivan admits that after life-threatening surgeries, atopic dermatitis seemed like a minor problem. Nevertheless, the family struggled with it for years without success.

The turning point was brought by his wife, a **Master of Pharmacy** by profession. When she saw that the conventional approach did not bring a solution, she decided to do something herself. At home, she made a **corticosteroid-free cream**, which they simply called "home cream" back then, and it helped Šimun.

The story then, as Ivan says, by God's providence and almost semi-consciously began to spread. Friends asked for the cream, then friends of friends, then their friends. Ivan returns to the thought from the beginning of the conversation that it takes him a long time to mature in certain things. Only after several years did it dawn on him: if the cream helps all these people, why wouldn't they make it widely available?

That is how **Astopic** was created. Ivan describes it as a Croatian product born out of a mother's love for her child. It is soon celebrating its first anniversary, and according to Ivan's words, it has already broken many records of the Croatian cosmetic industry:
- it is slowly entering export,
- it has a huge number of customers,
- it has gathered hundreds of positive reviews,
- it records constant growth, even though it is only at the beginning.

Ivan concludes that out of an adversity and a great problem God created something immeasurably blessed, and that became a successful family business.

sections.subtitle: Bog od smeća naših života radi remek-djelo
sections.screenshot_description: Gost, vidno dirnut, citira Richa Mullinsa o Bogu koji od smeća naših života stvara remek-djelo
sections.content:
Ivan Pokupec se u tom kontekstu uvijek sjeti riječi **Richa Mullinsa**, američkog autora duhovne glazbe. Prepričava snimku s YouTubea na kojoj Mullins prije jedne pjesme govori o svojoj mladosti. Kao melankoličnom tinejdžeru sklonom poeziji i tinejdžerskoj depresiji, stalno su mu govorili: „Ne brini, Bog te voli.“ On bi odgovarao da to samo znači da Bog nema ukusa, jer Bog voli sve, pa po čemu je onda on poseban. Kasnije je, kaže, shvatio što Bog radi: **„Bog uzima smeće naših života i od toga radi remek-djelo.“**

Ivan priznaje da se ježi dok to govori. Kaže da je Bog po tko zna koji put uzeo „smeće“ njihovih života: bolest, nemoć i beznađe.

Zatim opisuje osjećaj koji ne bi poželio nijednom roditelju. To je spoznaja da, koliko god novca, položaja ili moći imao, ne možeš pomoći vlastitom djetetu i možeš ga samo predati Bogu u ruke. Ivan je to proživio. Iz takvog beznađa, ljutnje, bijesa i ogorčenosti Bog je, kaže, izveo nešto što danas pomaže tisućama djece u Hrvatskoj.

Podsjeća na poznatu pjesmicu „Naš Bog je velik“ i dodaje da ljudi nemaju pojma koliko je velik. Zato je, prema njemu, potrebno svjedočanstvo: da ljudi vide koliko je Bog velik u njegovu životu i koliko još veći može biti u njihovu. Zaključuje porukom nade: **ne postoji bolest, ovisnost, prepreka, jad ni bijeda koju Otac ne može izvesti na dobro.**

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom o Božjoj providnosti: Bog može izvesti dobro iz zla i patnje, a kršćanska nada utemeljena je u Kristu, ne u uvjerenju da će svaka teškoća završiti željenim zemaljskim ishodom. Završna tvrdnja ipak traži pojašnjenje kako se ne bi shvatila kao obećanje ozdravljenja ili vidljivog uspjeha u svakom pojedinom slučaju.
concerns: Izraz „ne postoji bolest, ovisnost, prepreka, jad ni bijeda koju Otac ne može izvesti na dobro” u katoličkom je smislu prihvatljiv ako znači da Božja providnost može iz patnje izvesti dobro; bio bi problematičan ako bi sugerirao da će Bog uvijek ukloniti bolest, osigurati povoljan ishod ili da se dobro mora odmah vidjeti.

Metafora „smeća naših života” snažno izražava svjedočanstvo, ali može nenamjerno zvučati kao da su patnja i bolest same po sebi dobre ili da ljudska vrijednost ovisi o tome koliko je vidljivo korisnog proizašlo iz njih.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva uči da Bog ne uzrokuje zlo, ali ga dopušta te može iz njega izvesti dobro koje možda nećemo potpuno razumjeti u ovom životu; zato je nada utemeljena u Božjoj vjernosti i Kristovoj smrti i uskrsnuću, a ne u sigurnosti da će se nevolja riješiti na određeni način. Bolest može čovjeka dovesti do tjeskobe, očaja ili pobune, ali može potaknuti i zrelost, traženje Boga i usmjerenje na ono bitno. Stoga je svjedočanstvo o dobru koje je nastalo iz obiteljske patnje vrijedno, uz poštovanje činjenice da se Božji naum ne može uvijek prepoznati u ovom životu i da patnja nije sama po sebi dobro.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching on divine providence: God can bring good out of evil and suffering, and Christian hope is founded in Christ, not in the conviction that every hardship will end in a desired earthly outcome. The concluding claim nevertheless requires clarification so that it is not understood as a promise of healing or visible success in every individual case.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church teaches that God does not cause evil, but permits it and can bring good out of it that we may not fully understand in this life; therefore, hope is founded on God's faithfulness and Christ's death and resurrection, and not on the certainty that distress will be resolved in a specific way. Illness can lead a person to anguish, despair, or revolt, but it can also foster maturity, seeking God, and focusing on what is essential. Therefore, the testimony about the good that arose from family suffering is valuable, while respecting the fact that God's plan cannot always be recognized in this life and that suffering is not good in itself.
concerns_en: The phrase "there is no illness, addiction, obstacle, misery, nor wretchedness that the Father cannot bring about for good" is acceptable in the Catholic sense if it means that divine providence can bring good out of suffering; it would be problematic if it suggested that God will always remove illness, ensure a favorable outcome, or that the good must be immediately seen.

The metaphor of the "trash of our lives" strongly expresses testimony, but can unintentionally sound as though suffering and illness are good in themselves or that human worth depends on how much visibly useful came out of them.

sections.subtitle_en: God makes a masterpiece out of the trash of our lives
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest, visibly moved, quotes Rich Mullins about God making a masterpiece out of the trash of our lives
sections.content_en:
In this context, Ivan Pokupec always remembers the words of **Rich Mullins**, an American Christian music songwriter. He recounts a YouTube recording in which Mullins, before a song, speaks about his youth. As a melancholic teenager prone to poetry and teenage depression, they kept telling him: "Don't worry, God loves you." He would reply that this only means God has no taste, because God loves everything, so how is he special then. Later, he says, he realized what God does: **"God takes the trash of our lives and makes a masterpiece out of it."**

Ivan admits that he gets chills while saying this. He says that God has, for who knows which time, taken the "trash" of their lives: illness, helplessness, and hopelessness.

Then he describes a feeling he would not wish on any parent. It is the realization that, no matter how much money, status, or power you have, you cannot help your own child and can only surrender them into God's hands. Ivan lived through this. Out of such hopelessness, anger, rage, and resentment, God, he says, brought about something that today helps thousands of children in Hrvatska.

He recalls the well-known song "Our God is Great" and adds that people have no idea how great He is. That is why, according to him, testimony is needed: so that people see how great God is in his life and how even greater He can be in theirs. He concludes with a message of hope: **there is no illness, addiction, obstacle, misery, nor wretchedness that the Father cannot bring about for good.**

sections.subtitle: Blic pitanja: vjera u praksi, znak jednakosti i Ivan Krstitelj
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Pokupec se smije dok odgovara na provokativna ili-ili pitanja
sections.content:
Kruno ocjenjuje Ivanove misli kao prekrasne za kraj epizode, ali prije odjave postavlja nekoliko „ili-ili“ pitanja. Najavljuje da su pomalo provokativna, jer dobro zna kako gost razmišlja.

- **Teologija ili vjera u praksi?** Ivan bez zadrške odgovara: „Vjera u praksi. Točka. Nema dileme.“
- **SDP ili HDZ?** Kruno najavljuje da će ga ovo pitanje nasmijati. Ivan prvo pita mora li birati, a zatim kaže da bi između njih stavio „znak jednakosti, manje-više“. Kruno to proglašava najboljim odgovorom.
- **Sveti Petar ili sveti Pavao?** Nakon kratkog oklijevanja Ivan bira Pavla, „po svom karakteru“. Kruno priznaje da je to i očekivao.
- **Ivan Pernar ili Ivan Sinčić?** Ivan izbjegava izbor i odgovara: „Ivan Krstitelj.“ Kruno to naziva odličnim izborom.
- **Prisutnost u javnosti ili u obitelji?** Ivan bira obitelj, uz napomenu da se to nužno mora prelijevati i na javnost.
- **Osobno poduzetništvo ili sigurnost stalnog posla?** Ivan tvrdi da sigurnost stalnog posla danas ne postoji i bira poduzetništvo za svakoga tko ima „malo grifa“ za to. Kruno zaključuje da je to najbolje pokazao Ivanov vlastiti primjer.

magisterium.assessment: Odgovori su uglavnom spojivi s katoličkim naukom: naglašavanje praktičnog življenja vjere, obitelji i poduzetničke inicijative može biti pozitivno, a izbori svetih Pavla i Ivana Krstitelja ne iznose nikakvu spornu doktrinarnu tvrdnju. Ipak, riječ je pretežno o osobnim preferencijama, a tvrdnja da je poduzetništvo prikladno za svakoga tko ima „malo grifa“ pojednostavljuje različite pozive, sposobnosti i okolnosti.
concerns: Izbor „vjere u praksi“ može zvučati kao suprotstavljanje prakse teologiji, premda kršćansko djelovanje treba biti utemeljeno i prosvijetljeno istinom vjere.

Stavljanje SDP-a i HDZ-a gotovo na znak jednakosti nije samo po sebi katolički nauk, ali bez obrazloženja može zamagliti potrebu da se konkretne politike i kandidati prosuđuju prema moralnim načelima.
Preporuka poduzetništva „za svakoga“ tko ima grifa zanemaruje razlike u darovima, obiteljskim obvezama, ekonomikoj situaciji i rizicima.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk ne postavlja teologiju i praksu kao suparnice: vjera se očituje djelima, a kršćansko djelovanje treba biti oblikovano istinom vjere i odgovornošću za bližnje. Obitelj može biti temeljna zajednica vjere i služenja, ali njezina briga ne isključuje svjedočenje i služenje u javnom životu. Poduzetništvo može biti konkretan oblik služenja i svjedočenja, no poziv na poslovno djelovanje podrazumijeva odgovornost, a ne univerzalnu obvezu da svatko postane poduzetnik.

magisterium.assessment_en: The answers are mostly compatible with Catholic teaching: emphasizing the practical living of faith, family, and entrepreneurial initiative can be positive, and the choices of Saints Paul and John the Baptist do not put forward any controversial doctrinal claim. Nevertheless, it is predominantly a matter of personal preferences, and the claim that entrepreneurship is suitable for everyone who has „a little knack“ simplifies different vocations, abilities, and circumstances.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching does not set theology and practice as rivals: faith is manifested in works, and Christian action should be shaped by the truth of faith and responsibility for one's neighbors. The family can be the foundational community of faith and service, but care for it does not exclude witnessing and serving in public life. Entrepreneurship can be a concrete form of service and witness, but the vocation to business activity entails responsibility, rather than a universal obligation for everyone to become an entrepreneur.
concerns_en: The choice of „faith in practice“ may sound like opposing practice to theology, even though Christian action should be grounded in and enlightened by the truth of faith.

Putting SDP and HDZ almost at an equals sign is not in itself Catholic teaching, but without explanation it may obscure the need to judge concrete policies and candidates according to moral principles.
Recommending entrepreneurship „for everyone“ who has a knack neglects differences in gifts, family obligations, economic situations, and risks.

sections.subtitle_en: Quick-fire questions: faith in practice, equals sign, and John the Baptist
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Pokupec laughs while answering provocative either-or questions
sections.content_en:
Kruno assesses Ivan's thoughts as wonderful for the end of the episode, but before signing off he asks a few "either-or" questions. He announces that they are somewhat provocative, because he knows well how the guest thinks.

- **Theology or faith in practice?** Ivan answers without hesitation: „Faith in practice. Period. There is no dilemma.“
- **SDP or HDZ?** Kruno announces that this question will make him laugh. Ivan first asks if he has to choose, and then says that between them he would put „an equals sign, more or less“. Kruno declares that the best answer.
- **Saint Peter or Saint Paul?** After a short hesitation Ivan chooses Paul, „according to his character“. Kruno admits that he expected that as well.
- **Ivan Pernar or Ivan Sinčić?** Ivan avoids the choice and answers: „John the Baptist.“ Kruno calls that an excellent choice.
- **Presence in public or in the family?** Ivan chooses family, with the note that this must necessarily spill over into the public as well.
- **Personal entrepreneurship or the security of a permanent job?** Ivan claims that the security of a permanent job does not exist today and chooses entrepreneurship for anyone who has „a little knack“ for it. Kruno concludes that this was best demonstrated by Ivan's own example.

sections.subtitle: „Muževni budite“: odjava i najava sljedeće epizode
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Pokupec zahvaljuje voditelju i poručuje „muževni budite“
sections.content:
Kruno zahvaljuje gostu na vremenu. Kaže da je razgovor lijepo tekao i da su pokrili sve što je smatrao važnim, s obzirom na to da se jako dobro poznaju. Za kraj pita gdje se Ivan vidi za deset godina.

Ivan odgovara da se vidi **u Božjoj milosti**, kao i dosad. Vraća se slici s početka priče: i dalje planira biti voljeni sin i „Mujo“ kojeg će Bog uvijek primiti za kragnu i staviti na pravo mjesto u pravo vrijeme. To mu je, kaže, sve što u životu treba, a sve drugo može otići.

Kruno se veseli Ivanovim budućim „avanturama“ i najavljuje da će u tome blisko surađivati. Ivan uzvraća da je veliki blagoslov imati suborca poput njega i oprašta se porukom koja nosi ime emisije: **„Muževni budite.“**

Kruno to naziva najboljom porukom za kraj. Zahvaljuje gledateljima na praćenju druge epizode i poziva ih da lajkaju, dijele i pretplate se na kanal te da emisiju prate na **Patreonu**, gdje se epizode mogu pogledati i prije redovnog emitiranja. Odjavljuje se riječima „Vidimo se u sljedećoj Redefiniciji“, a Ivan pozdravlja publiku i zahvaljuje ekipi iza kamere.

### Isječak iz sljedeće epizode

Na samom kraju prikazan je kratak isječak sugovornika iz sljedeće epizode. On preporučuje knjigu **„Sanjajte i snovi će nadići realnost“**, koju je napisao prijatelj **svetog Josemaríje Escrive**. Objašnjava da knjiga opisuje istinite događaje, odnosno poticaje koje je Escrivá imao prije osnivanja **Opusa Dei**, Djela Božjega. Ono što je počelo kao ideja tijekom jednog razmatranja danas je, kaže sugovornik, velika struktura u Crkvi i „jedna dobra kičma muževnosti u Crkvi“.

magisterium.assessment: Izraz povjerenja u Božju milost i providnost te poticaj „Muževni budite“ mogu se razumjeti u skladu s kršćanskim pozivom na svetost, odgovornost i ljubav, a u odlomku nema jasnog proturječja katoličkom nauku. Ipak, govor o tome da će Bog Ivana „staviti na pravo mjesto“ i neobjašnjeni pojam muževnosti ostaju slikoviti i otvoreni za tumačenje, pa ih ne treba shvatiti kao poziv na pasivnost ili kao opravdanje stereotipa.
concerns: Slika Božjeg djelovanja može, ako se shvati doslovno ili fatalistički, zamagliti ljudsku slobodu i odgovornost; katoličko razumijevanje providnosti uključuje suradnju čovjeka s Božjim naumom.

„Muževni budite“ i opis Opusa Dei kao „kičme muževnosti“ nisu sami po sebi problematični, ali bez pojašnjenja mogu suziti kršćansku muževnost na kulturni ideal koji ne obuhvaća služenje, nježnost i poštovanje dostojanstva žena.
Odlomak prenosi tvrdnju o poticajima koje je sveti Josemaría imao prije osnivanja Opusa Dei, ali dostupni izvori ne omogućuju procjenu njezine povijesne točnosti.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk uči da providnost djeluje i kroz postupke stvorenja te da Bog čovjeku daje mogućnost slobodne suradnje sa svojim naumom; pouzdanje u Boga stoga ne znači odustajanje od djelovanja i odgovornosti. Kršćanska muževnost osobito se očituje u ljubavi koja se daruje: muž je pozvan ljubiti kao Krist, poštovati jednako dostojanstvo žene te odgovorno skrbiti za obitelj. Crkveni opis karizme Opusa Dei ističe posvećivanje običnog profesionalnog rada i apostolat u svakodnevnim okolnostima; to daje sadržajniji smisao izrazu „kičma muževnosti“ ako se njime misli na vjernost, služenje i svetost u životu i radu.
magisterium.assessment_en: The expression of trust in God's grace and providence and the encouragement „Be manly“ can be understood in accordance with the Christian call to holiness, responsibility, and love, and in the passage there is no clear contradiction to Catholic teaching. Nevertheless, the talk of God putting Ivan „in the right place“ and the unexplained concept of manliness remain figurative and open to interpretation, so they should not be understood as a call to passivity or as a justification of stereotypes.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching teaches that providence also acts through the actions of creatures and that God gives man the possibility of free cooperation with His plan; trust in God therefore does not mean giving up on action and responsibility. Christian manliness is especially manifested in self-giving love: the husband is called to love like Christ, to respect the equal dignity of woman, and to responsibly care for the family. The Church's description of the charism of Opus Dei emphasizes the sanctification of ordinary professional work and apostolate in everyday circumstances; this gives a more substantive meaning to the phrase „backbone of manliness“ if it refers to fidelity, service, and holiness in life and work.
concerns_en: The image of God's action can, if understood literally or fatalistically, obscure human freedom and responsibility; the Catholic understanding of providence includes man's cooperation with God's plan.

„Be manly“ and the description of Opus Dei as the „backbone of manliness“ are not problematic in themselves, but without clarification they can narrow Christian manliness to a cultural ideal that does not encompass service, tenderness, and respect for the dignity of women.
The passage conveys a claim about the promptings that Saint Josemaría had before the founding of Opus Dei, but available sources do not allow an assessment of its historical accuracy.

sections.subtitle_en: „Be manly“: sign-off and announcement of the next episode
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Pokupec thanks the host and says „be manly“
sections.content_en:
Kruno thanks the guest for his time. He says that the conversation flowed nicely and that they covered everything he considered important, considering that they know each other very well. For the end, he asks where Ivan sees himself in ten years.

Ivan answers that he sees himself **in God's grace**, as up to now. He returns to the image from the beginning of the story: he still plans to be a beloved son and a „Mujo“ whom God will always take by the collar and put in the right place at the right time. That is, he says, everything he needs in life, and everything else can go.

Kruno looks forward to Ivan's future „adventures“ and announces that they will collaborate closely on that. Ivan replies that it is a great blessing to have a fellow fighter like him and bids farewell with the message that bears the name of the show: **„Be manly.“**

Kruno calls that the best message for the end. He thanks the viewers for following the second episode and invites them to like, share, and subscribe to the channel and to follow the show on **Patreon**, where episodes can also be watched before regular broadcasting. He signs off with the words „See you in the next Redefinicija“, and Ivan greets the audience and thanks the crew behind the camera.

### Clip from the next episode

At the very end, a short clip of the interlocutor from the next episode is shown. He recommends the book **„Dream and Dreams Will Outgrow Reality“**, written by a friend of **Saint Josemaría Escrivá**. He explains that the book describes true events, that is, the promptings that Escrivá had before the founding of **Opus Dei**, the Work of God. What began as an idea during one meditation is today, the interlocutor says, a large structure in the Church and „a good backbone of manliness in the Church“.
